head: f5bef37
target: AGENTS.md sets the rules for the one plugin tree, above all two contracts: hook scripts find the plugin root from their own path, never from CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, and every hooks/hooks.json edit must tell Codex users to rerun scripts/codex-trust-hooks.
incidental: README.md: it documents the install, opt-in, and update flows the code already has
CLAUDE.md: a symlink to AGENTS.md, so Claude Code reads the same rules
the selftest step: run scripts/selftest after changing anything under skills/ or hooks/
the validate step: run claude plugin validate . after changing a manifest
the version bump step: bump version in .claude-plugin/plugin.json so installs pick the change up

questions.prompt: Why do hook scripts find the plugin root with dirname "$0" and not with CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT from the environment?

options.label: Codex removes the variable from hook processes, so scripts that read it fail there.
Git runs hooks with a clean environment, so plugin variables never reach the script.
Droid sets the variable to a placeholder inside hook processes, so it names a root that is not real there. The script's own path is real in every harness.
The plugin tree can be cloned anywhere, so no environment variable can ever point to it.

key_points: Droid gives hook processes a placeholder value, so the variable names a root that is not real there
dirname "$0" follows the script's real location, so one script serves Claude Code, Droid, and Codex
the rule keeps hooks free of harness-specific code

questions.prompt: A new hook script builds its paths from CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT. Which of these are true?

options.label: Under Droid, the variable holds a placeholder, so the hook builds paths under a root that is not real.
A test that the variable is set and not empty would catch the failure.
The hook can still work under Claude Code, so work done there can miss the break.
Taking the root from dirname "$0" instead makes the same script work under all three harnesses.

key_points: the failure hits Droid only: the placeholder names a root that is not real
the variable is set, not missing, so an empty-value test does not catch it
the break can stay hidden while the hook works under Claude Code

questions.prompt: A new hook entry lands in hooks/hooks.json, and the hook script reads a file inside the plugin tree. What must the change get right for all three harnesses, and why?
key_points: the script finds the plugin root with dirname "$0", not CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, because Droid sets that variable to a placeholder inside hook processes
the change tells Codex users to rerun scripts/codex-trust-hooks, because an edit to hooks/hooks.json changes its Codex trust hash
Codex skips plugin hooks until their definitions are trusted again
